title: Choose and evaluate models · Level 1
slo: Choose a model approach for a task and explain how Foundry evaluates models.

exercises.question_text: Which task-to-model matches are correct? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: text-embedding-3-small is an embedding model. Embedding models are built for semantic vector representations.
GPT-5.1-codex is listed as a recommended model type for coding. It supports the coding task category.
Phi-4-multimodal-instruct is listed for multimodal work. Multimodal chat can include images, audio, and video.

options.error_type: Confuses chat model with embedding model
options.rationale: GPT-4.1 is optimized for real-time chat and customer support. Embeddings require an embedding model such as text-embedding-3-small.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-4.1 for fast interactive chat at scale.

feedback.intrinsic: Search by meaning would not be matched to the model type built for semantic vectors.
feedback.instructional: Task type matters. Use embedding models for semantic vector representations and GPT-4.1 for real-time chat.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Each selected pairing matches the model type to the task it is recommended for.

exercises.question_text: Which model is described as an Anthropic frontier-level model?

options.rationale: Claude Opus 4.5 is described as an Anthropic frontier-level model. It is intended for sophisticated agents and difficult reasoning tasks.
GPT-5.x is optimized for reasoning, planning, and agentic workflows. It is not the Anthropic model named here.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-5.x for structured logic, multi-step reasoning, and adjustable thinking levels.

feedback.intrinsic: A team needing the stated Anthropic option would begin evaluating the wrong family.
feedback.instructional: Keep the model names distinct: Claude Opus 4.5 is the Anthropic frontier-level choice.

options.error_type: Confuses general-purpose model with frontier agent model
options.rationale: Mistral Large 3 is a general-purpose model that balances quality, throughput, cost, and latency. It is not described as Anthropic’s frontier-level model.
options.better_fit: Choose Mistral Large 3 for balanced multilingual drafting or business-report work.

feedback.intrinsic: The selection would emphasize balance rather than the specified frontier-level capability.
feedback.instructional: Mistral Large 3 is a different model with a different focus. The Anthropic frontier-level model is Claude Opus 4.5.

options.error_type: Confuses real-time chat model with frontier model
options.rationale: GPT-4.1 is optimized for responsive, high-volume chat. It is not the Anthropic frontier-level model.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-4.1 for real-time chat, customer support, and interactive applications.

feedback.intrinsic: The choice would favor fast scale instead of the requested sophisticated-agent work.
feedback.instructional: GPT-4.1 and Claude Opus 4.5 solve different needs. The latter is the frontier-level Anthropic option.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Claude Opus 4.5 is the Anthropic frontier-level model in this set.

exercises.question_text: Text-embedding-3-small is built mainly for generating chat replies.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A search-by-meaning feature could be designed around the wrong task type.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Embedding models represent meaning as vectors. Use chat models when the main task is generating conversational replies.

exercises.explanation: Correct. text-embedding-3-small is built for semantic vector representations, not primarily chat replies.

exercises.question_text: Claude Opus 4.5 can suit complex code reasoning and multi-step computer-use tasks.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That choice could steer a long, complex task toward a model selected for a different strength.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Claude Opus 4.5 is suited to sophisticated agents, difficult code reasoning, and multi-step computer-use tasks.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Complex code reasoning and multi-step computer use are stated strengths of Claude Opus 4.5.

exercises.question_text: Which uses fit Mistral Large 3? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Mistral Large 3 is suitable for multilingual drafting. This is one of its stated general-purpose uses.
Mistral Large 3 can support structured business report generation. This fits its balance of quality and efficient throughput.
Mistral Large 3 can fit mid-latency agent tasks. It is positioned for balanced cost and performance.

options.error_type: Confuses Mistral Large 3 with GPT-4.1 focus
options.rationale: Mistral Large 3 has broader general-purpose uses than customer chat alone. Real-time customer support is a stated strength of GPT-4.1.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-4.1 for real-time chat and high-volume customer support.

feedback.intrinsic: A team could unnecessarily limit a balanced general-purpose model to one narrow workload.
feedback.instructional: Mistral Large 3 supports several kinds of work. GPT-4.1 is the model optimized for speedy support chat.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These are stated uses for Mistral Large 3’s balanced general-purpose capabilities.

options.rationale: A model family contains related models that share architecture or lineage. Members can still differ in size, capability, specialization, or version.
An endpoint is created when a configured model is deployed. It is not a group of related models.
options.better_fit: Use this phrase when describing how an application calls a deployed model.

feedback.intrinsic: This would make it harder to compare related model choices before deployment.
feedback.instructional: Separate the group from the deployment: a family is related models, while deployment makes one configured model available.

options.text: A group sold directly by Azure
options.rationale: Models sold directly by Azure are one catalog source. A family is defined by shared lineage, not by who sells it.
options.better_fit: Use this when comparing Azure-sold models with partner or community models.

feedback.intrinsic: You could overlook related models that come from a different catalog source.
feedback.instructional: Provider source and model lineage answer different questions. A family describes related architecture or history.

options.error_type: Confuses a family with model input
options.rationale: A prompt is input sent to a model. It is not a collection of related models.
options.better_fit: Use this when describing a request sent to a model.

feedback.intrinsic: You would be naming the request instead of the group of models.
feedback.instructional: Remember that a family groups models; a prompt supplies input to one model.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A family groups related models, even when members differ in size or capability.

exercises.question_text: Mistral Large 3 is designed only for high-volume, low-latency production chat.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That choice could restrict a model’s use to fast chat even when multilingual drafting or business reports are needed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The high-volume, low-latency focus describes GPT-4.1. Mistral Large 3 is broader and balances several trade-offs.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Mistral Large 3 is a general-purpose model that balances quality, throughput, cost, and latency.

exercises.question_text: Foundation models are large pretrained models that can provide general capabilities out of the box.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That choice would rule out a ready-to-deploy base model for a general task.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Foundation models are large pretrained models. They can be deployed immediately or customized through fine-tuning.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Foundation models already provide general language, reasoning, or multimodal capabilities.

exercises.question_text: Which model is available to all Foundry users?

options.rationale: GPT-4.1 is stated as available to all Foundry users. It is also optimized for responsive chat at scale.
GPT-5 model-family availability is currently restricted by registration. It is not the all-user option.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-5.x when registration is available and multi-step reasoning or planning is needed.

feedback.intrinsic: A team could plan for a model family before confirming that registration is complete.
feedback.instructional: Availability matters during selection. GPT-4.1 is available to all Foundry users, while GPT-5.x requires registration.

options.error_type: Confuses Anthropic model with Foundry availability note
options.rationale: Claude Opus 4.5 is identified for frontier-level complex work. The all-user availability statement applies to GPT-4.1.
options.better_fit: Choose Claude Opus 4.5 for long-context complex code reasoning or computer-use tasks.

feedback.intrinsic: The team might mistake a capability description for the specific availability note.
feedback.instructional: Keep availability separate from capability. GPT-4.1 is the model explicitly available to all Foundry users.

options.error_type: Confuses catalog availability with all-user availability
options.rationale: Mistral Large 3 is a balanced general-purpose catalog model. The all-user availability statement names GPT-4.1 instead.
options.better_fit: Choose Mistral Large 3 for multilingual drafting or balanced quality, cost, and latency.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could confuse being in the catalog with the stated all-user access detail.
feedback.instructional: Catalog presence and the all-user availability note are different. The noted model is GPT-4.1.

exercises.explanation: Correct. GPT-4.1 is the model explicitly available to all Foundry users.

exercises.question_text: Which are strengths of GPT-5.x? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: GPT-5.x is optimized for multi-step reasoning. This supports work that needs several connected reasoning steps.
Structured logic and planning are stated strengths of GPT-5.x. These strengths suit complex, organized work.
GPT-5.x supports adjustable thinking levels. They let developers trade speed for accuracy.
This is the main optimization of GPT-4.1. GPT-5.x is described for reasoning, logic, planning, and agentic workflows.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-4.1 for real-time chat and high-volume production workloads.

feedback.intrinsic: Choosing for this reason could slow a busy customer-support experience.
feedback.instructional: Match GPT-5.x to reasoning-heavy work. Match GPT-4.1 to speed, efficiency, and low-latency scale.

exercises.explanation: Correct. GPT-5.x combines reasoning, planning, and adjustable thinking levels.

exercises.question_text: GPT-4.1 is optimized for speed, efficiency, and low-latency inference.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A fast interactive workload could be matched to a model chosen for deeper reasoning instead.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: GPT-4.1 is optimized for speed, efficiency, and low-latency inference, especially at production scale.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These strengths make GPT-4.1 suitable for responsive, high-volume applications.

exercises.question_text: GPT-5.x is available to all Foundry users without registration.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A team could plan around a model family before confirming that it is available to them.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: GPT-5.x currently requires registration. GPT-4.1 is the model stated as available to all Foundry users.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Registration currently restricts access to the GPT-5 model family.

flashcards.back: Related models sharing lineage but differing in size, capability, specialization, or version.
For multi-step reasoning, planning, and agentic workflows.
For complex agents, code reasoning, and long-context tasks.
Real-time, high-volume chat with speed and low latency.
